title: Basics
body: A jq program is a filter: it takes JSON values in and produces zero or more JSON values out. `.` is the identity filter (the input, unchanged). Filters combine with `|` (pipe: the left side's outputs become the right side's inputs) and `,` (both sides' outputs, one after the other). Every expression is a filter, including literals: `1` outputs 1 whatever the input.

title: Paths: .foo, .[n], .[]
body: `.foo` is the value at key foo (null if missing; an error on a non-object). `.foo.bar` goes deeper. `."key with spaces"` or `.["key"]` for awkward keys. `.[2]` is an array element (negative counts from the end), `.[2:4]` a slice. `.[]` outputs every element of an array (or every value of an object), one at a time. A `?` after any of these suppresses errors: `.foo?`, `.[]?`.

title: Pipe and comma
body: `a | b` runs b on each output of a. `a, b` outputs a's results then b's. Parentheses group: `(.a, .b) | length`. Comma binds tighter than pipe.

title: Building values
body: Arrays: `[ f ]` collects every output of f into one array (`[.[] | .name]`). Objects: `{a: .x, "b": 1}`; shorthand `{name}` means `{name: .name}`; a key in parentheses is computed: `{(.k): .v}`. If a value filter has several outputs, the object is built once for each.

title: Conditionals and comparisons
body: `if c then a elif d then b else e end` (`else` is optional in 1.7, meaning `.`). `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` compare any JSON values. `and`, `or`, `not` (not is a filter: `. | not`). Only false and null are falsey; 0 and "" are true. `a // b` is the alternative operator: a's outputs that aren't false or null, else b.

title: Built-in functions
body: jq has many built-ins; look each one up with `symbol NAME`. They take their arguments as filters, separated by `;` (not `,`): `sub("a"; "b")`.

title: Defining functions and variables
body: `def name: body;` or `def name(f; g): body;`; arguments are filters. `$__loc__` and `$ENV` are built in. `expr as $x | body` binds a variable for the body (once per output of expr). Destructuring: `. as {a: $x, b: [$y]} | ...`. `reduce .[] as $x (init; update)` folds; `foreach` emits each step.

title: Strings and formats
body: Interpolation: `"Hello \(.name)"`. Format strings: `@base64`, `@base64d`, `@uri`, `@csv`, `@tsv`, `@html`, `@sh`, `@json`, `@text`; applied as filters (`@csv`) or before a string to format interpolations (`@uri "q=\(.q)"`). Regexes (Oniguruma): `test`, `match`, `capture`, `sub`, `gsub`, `split/2`.

title: Running jq
body: `jq [options] FILTER [files...]`. Input is a stream of JSON values (from files or stdin); the filter runs on each. See `tool jq` for the options.
